answer: The cheapest real defence: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because lagoon only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, quill is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any dune approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
